sentences.text:
----Applicant Versus
1. State Of Rajasthan
2. Seenu D/o Bhanaram, R/o Dhadhamta, P.S. Kotada, District Udaipur (Raj.)
----Respondents For Applicant(s) : Ms. Deepika Purohit For Respondent(s) : Mr. Sarwan Kumar
Bishnoi, Public Prosecutor Justice Dinesh Mehta Order 15/01/2024
1.

This application for bail has been filed by the applicant under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,1973 in connection with FIR No.69/23, Police Station Mandawa, District Udaipur for the offences under sections 366, 342, 376 & 506 of the Indian Penal Code,1860.
2.

While maintaining that the FIR in question is false and has been lodged in order to unnecessarily harass the present applicant, learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the delay in lodging the FIR suggests that the same is false.

3. Learned counsel invited court's attention towards the contents of FIR, the statements of the prosecutrix under sections 161 and 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and [2024:RJ-JD:2150] (2 of 4) [CRLMB-140/2024] highlighted that the stand/version of the prosecutrix is different at all the stages of recording of evidence.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that there is inconsistency in the stand of the prosecutrix, hence, the applicant who is behind bars since 21.09.2023, be enlarged on bail.
5. Learned Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the bail application.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record including the FIR, statements of the prosecutrix under sections 161 and 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,1973.

sentences.text: 7 . On comparative analysis of the FIR and the statements of the prosecutrix under section 161 and 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, this Court finds that firstly the FIR came to be lodged on 03.09.2023 in relation to an incident which purportedly took place on 02.08.2023.
In the written report, the complainant stated that she was going to Dhadhamta from her native house/parent's house (Khajuriya) when the incident took place.

While in her statement under section 161, which were recorded on 06.09.2023, she claimed the incident to be of six months back, while stating that the same happened when she was going to purchase households goods in Kotada.

8. It is to be noted that in her statement under section 161, the prosecutrix has accepted the factum of friendship between the applicant and herself while in her statement under section 164, she has totally denied her acquaintance with the applicant.

9. It is also to be noted that in her statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 recorded on 12.09.2023, [2024:RJ-JD:2150] (3 of 4) [CRLMB-140/2024] the prosecutrix has stated that she was standing on Khajuria Road and was going to Dhadhamta, when the present applicant has approached her with jeep and promised to drop at Dhadhamta and enroute, the applicant had committed sexual assault (rape).
10.

The different versions of the prosecutrix in her statements recorded under sections 161 & 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 raises serious doubt about her story and commission of sexual assault upon her.
That apart, the delay of one month in lodging FIR without any justifiable reason is also a relevant factor in the case in hands.
11. This Court, therefore, deems it just and proper to grant bail to the accused-applicant under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

12. Consequently, the bail application filed under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 is allowed.

The applicant Ramesh Kumar S/o Jethiya, arrested in connection with FIR No.69/23, Police Station Mandawa, District Udaipur shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
13. Applicant shall be required to appear before that Court on all dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so.
14. Needless to mention that the above observations made by this Court are on the basis of material so far produced before the Court.

These are only prima-facie observations and the same shall however, not come in the way of the trial Court to take [2024:RJ-JD:2150] (4 of 4)
[CRLMB-140/2024] independent view of the matter, based on ocular and oral evidence, while finally deciding the case.

(DINESH MEHTA),J 53-himanshu/-
